findings.evidence: Gotcha 'Bump `version` on every element you change.' repeats worker contract step 3 (line 57) 'On each changed element, bump `version` and set a new random `versionNonce`', and the `edit --relabel` sentence on line 85 repeats line 43's command note
findings.fix: Keep the full rule in one place: leave the reason (collaboration sync keeps the higher version) in the Gotchas and shorten worker step 3 to 'Follow the version/seed/id gotchas below for every changed or new element'

findings.evidence: The route table handles `.excalidraw.md` (Obsidian plugin) files, but the description never names them, so a request about an Obsidian Excalidraw drawing will not trigger the skill
findings.fix: Create, inspect, edit and compare Excalidraw diagrams (.excalidraw, .excalidraw.json) through a bundled script that keeps scene JSON out of context - label and connection summaries, add/rename/remove boxes and arrows, binding and ID validation, label-level diffs. Use when the user names an Excalidraw file, asks to change labels or connections in one, compares two, or wants a flowchart or architecture sketch in Excalidraw, even for a tiny file; also covers .excalidraw.png and .excalidraw.svg files with an embedded scene and Obsidian .excalidraw.md drawings. Not for Mermaid, draw.io, PlantUML, Graphviz, ordinary PNG edits or text-only architecture explanations.

findings.evidence: 'New diagram | write a spec, `new SPEC -o OUT`': write() in scene.py replaces OUT unconditionally (tmp.replace(out)). If the user names an existing file for a 'new' diagram, it is silently overwritten, and the skill says nothing about where to put the spec file or whether to delete it
findings.fix: Add to the `new` bullet (line 42): 'If OUT already exists, ask before overwriting it, or write to a new name and `diff` it against the existing file. Write SPEC to a temporary path and delete it after `new` succeeds.'

findings.evidence: preservation() iterates only 'for e in old["elements"]:' and compares elements through an ID-indexed dictionary. An unrelated new element or a reordering of existing elements therefore passes diff --strict. In the worker route, an accidental standalone-text insertion or stacking-order change can pass both validation gates and be promoted over the original.
findings.fix: Check added IDs against an explicit creation allowlist and preserve the relative order of untouched elements. Track intended new elements and their text in TOUCHED so legitimate additions still pass. Add regression cases for unrelated insertions and reordering.

findings.evidence: '"free_text": [e.get("text", "") for e in els if e.get("type") == "text" and not e.get("containerId")]' omits IDs, while diff() compares only shapes and connections. Two identical standalone labels cannot use the documented ambiguous-label fallback, and a successful standalone-text relabel produces an empty diff.
findings.fix: Return standalone text as ID/text records, expose those IDs for ambiguous-label resolution, and include standalone-text additions, removals and relabels in diff output. Update the command documentation accordingly.

findings.evidence: 'edge_point(a, cb), edge_point(b, ca)' returns the same center point for a self-loop. The accepted spec {"nodes":["Retry"],"edges":[["Retry","Retry"]]} consequently writes a zero-width, zero-height arrow with coincident points; check and summary still report success.
findings.fix: Generate nondegenerate self-loop geometry with distinct outline endpoints, or reject self-loops before writing and document a supported fallback. Add a regression assertion that an accepted retry loop has nonzero visible geometry.

findings.evidence: 'Keep every other element byte-for-byte, plus appState, files and top-level metadata' is unconditional, although the routing table sends image operations to the worker. Adding a new image requires adding its data to files, but the contract and strict preservation check prohibit that necessary change.
findings.fix: Permit narrowly scoped files changes for explicitly requested image additions or replacements, backed by per-file-ID preservation allowances and reference validation. Likewise, allow only explicitly requested appState fields for canvas changes, retaining strict preservation for everything unrelated.
